title: How Long Does Business Funding Take?
seo_title: How Long Does Business Funding Take? Timelines | Fidelity Funding
meta_description: How long business funding takes by product: working capital, lines of credit, equipment financing, factoring and SBA loans, plus what slows each one down.
primary_keyword: how long does business funding take
keywords: how long does business funding take
dek: Speed depends far more on the product and your paperwork than on any single lender. Here is what the clock usually looks like.
intro: Your walk-in cooler died on Tuesday and the replacement quote expires Friday. Or your biggest customer pays in 60 days and payroll is in nine. In both cases the first question is the same: how fast can money actually arrive?

The honest answer is a range. Some working-capital products can move from application to funds in a day or two, while an SBA loan can take weeks or months. This guide lays out typical timelines by product, explains where the time goes, and offers practical ways to shorten it, with the caveat that nobody can guarantee a date.

sections.h2: The stages every application passes through
paragraphs: Regardless of product, funding follows roughly the same path: application, document collection, underwriting review, offer, acceptance and signing, then disbursement. What varies is how much each stage demands.

Fast products compress the middle. They rely on bank statements and revenue data that can be checked quickly, then use e-signature and electronic transfer. Slower products add steps like appraisals, tax verification, collateral filings and committee approval. Knowing which stage you are in helps you see what to do next.

Think of the stages as a relay. A delay at any handoff, whether a missing page, a slow callback or a late signature, pushes everything after it. The owner who keeps each handoff short usually sees the shortest total timeline.
These are general patterns, not promises. Each funding partner has its own process, and timing varies by funding partner and underwriting.
bullets: Merchant cash advances and short-term working capital: decisions often within hours, funding often within 24 hours once approved
Business lines of credit: from a few days to a couple of weeks, depending on the provider and documents
Equipment financing: often days to a couple of weeks, depending on the vendor paperwork
Invoice factoring: setup may take several days, and later advances on new invoices can be much quicker
Term loans from banks: commonly several weeks
SBA loans: commonly several weeks to a few months

sections.h2: Why SBA and bank loans are slower
paragraphs: These programs are built to be low-cost and well documented, and the paperwork reflects it. You may need multiple years of tax returns, a business plan, personal financial statements, collateral details and sometimes environmental or appraisal reports. Banks also have internal credit committees and have to meet program rules.

That is not a flaw. If you can wait and your profile fits, the cost can be much lower than faster products. The comparison between time and cost is covered in our guide on SBA versus alternative lending.

sections.h2: What slows things down on your end
paragraphs: Most delays are self-inflicted and fixable. A few come up again and again: partial bank statements, an ID that has expired, names that do not match across documents, unexplained large deposits, and an owner who cannot be reached for a verification call. Another common one is signing late in the day on a Friday, since transfers may not clear until the next business day.

Weekends and bank holidays also matter. A deal that closes Thursday afternoon may fund Friday, while one that closes Friday evening may not show up until Monday or Tuesday. If timing is critical, plan around the calendar.

Verification calls deserve special mention. Many funding partners confirm basic details by phone or text before releasing money, and an unanswered call can sit in a queue for a day. Tell your specialist the best number and hours to reach you, and watch for messages from unfamiliar numbers during the process.

sections.h2: How to move faster, step by step
paragraphs: You cannot control a funder's queue, but you can control your side of the process.
steps: Gather four to six months of complete bank statements and owner ID before you apply.
Make sure your business name, address and EIN match across every document.
Answer the specialist's call or text quickly, since verification often waits on you.
Write down the reason for any unusual deposit, overdraft or existing financing.
Be clear about the amount and the purpose, and when the money must arrive.
Review offers promptly and sign electronically as soon as you are comfortable.

sections.h2: Fast is not the only criterion
paragraphs: When cash is tight, speed can feel like everything. It is worth pausing long enough to compare total payback, payment schedule and any fees, since faster products usually cost more than slower ones. A good rule is to ask what happens if you wait one more week, and whether a cheaper product could arrive in time.

With Fidelity Funding, you complete a short application, a soft credit pull handles the initial review without affecting your score, and a funding specialist walks through the options with you, including how long each is likely to take. Many decisions arrive within hours and funding can follow in as little as a day after approval, though no timing is guaranteed and it depends on the funding partner and the completeness of your file.

It also helps to ask each funding partner what their typical turnaround is after signing, because disbursement methods differ. Some send funds by ACH that posts the next business day, while others may support faster delivery. Knowing the method in advance lets you plan payroll or a supplier deadline around the real arrival date, not the optimistic one.

key_takeaways: Working-capital products are often the fastest, with decisions in hours and funding often within a day after approval.
Bank loans and SBA programs usually take weeks to months because of heavier documentation.
Incomplete or mismatched paperwork is the most common cause of delay.
Bank holidays and weekends can add days between signing and receiving funds.
Speed usually costs more, so compare total payback before choosing.

faq.q: Can I really get business funding in 24 hours?
faq.a: Sometimes. Certain working-capital products can fund within about a day after approval when documents are complete and the funding partner moves quickly. It is not guaranteed and it varies by funding partner, product and underwriting. Larger or more complex requests generally take longer.

faq.q: Why did my approved funding take several more days?
faq.a: After approval, steps like contract signing, identity or bank verification, lien filings and bank transfer processing still apply. Weekends and holidays also pause transfers. Responding quickly and signing early in the business day can shorten this stage.

faq.q: How long does an SBA loan take?
faq.a: Commonly several weeks to a few months from application to funding, depending on the lender, the program and how quickly you supply documents. It can be a good fit when cost matters more than speed. Timelines vary and are not guaranteed.

faq.q: Does applying through a broker make funding slower?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A broker can shorten the search by matching your profile to suitable funding partners and preparing a complete file. Timing still depends on each partner's underwriting and on how fast you provide documents and sign.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to get an offer?
faq.a: Apply with complete, recent bank statements, a valid ID and consistent business details, and be reachable for follow-up questions. Clear answers about amount and purpose also help a specialist narrow to the right partners sooner.
